nodes.description: The defining finding. The ejaculate contains mostly headless flagella and a minority of tail-less heads; one patient had 98% acephalic spermatozoa. In the knockout mouse the headless tails carry a retained cytoplasmic droplet and can be mistaken for round-headed sperm.

evidence.snippet: Acephalic spermatozoa syndrome (ASS) is a rare but extremely severe type of teratozoospermia, defined by the presence of a majority of headless flagella and a minority of tail-less sperm heads in the ejaculate.

nodes.description: The head-tail coupling apparatus assembles normally early in spermiogenesis, but without SUN5 it detaches with the basal plate from the implantation fossa as the spermatid elongates. The centrosome and coupling apparatus drift away from the nucleus, and head and tail separate once the manchette disappears. The break lies between the nucleus and the proximal centriole, so the headless tails keep both centrioles and the heads lack an implantation fossa and basal plate.

evidence.reference_title: Essential role for SUN5 in anchoring sperm head to the tail.
evidence.snippet: Ultrastructural studies of spermatogenesis in Sun5−/− male mice revealed that the sperm head-tail coupling apparatus could be successfully assembled during the early stage of spermiogenesis, but without functional SUN5, the coupling apparatus together with the basal plate disassociated from the implantation fossa during the elongation of the spermatids.

evidence.snippet: Furthermore, ultrastructural imaging revealed that the head-tail coupling apparatus (HTCA) and the centrosome were distant from the nucleus at steps 9-10 during spermatid elongation. With the manchette disappearing at steps 13-14, the head and the tail segregated.

evidence.snippet: Our results, together with those of the previous study, show that SUN5 is required for the formation of the sperm head-tail junction and male fertility.

nodes.description: At the posterior nuclear envelope SUN5 binds partners on both sides of the envelope: lamin B1 inside the nucleus, and the KASH protein Nesprin3, the centriole-associated septin SEPTIN12, ODF1 and the linker CENTLEIN outside it. Cryo-electron tomography of mammalian sperm shows a regular hexagonal protein lattice in the nuclear envelope at the base of the head, proposed to be formed by these LINC complexes. Losing SUN5 dissolves this complex and Nesprin3 loses its posterior localization. The partner data come mainly from Sun5 knockout mice and transfected cells, with altered Nesprin3 and ODF1 staining confirmed in patient sperm.

evidence.snippet: Further coimmunoprecipitation (Co-IP) and immunofluorescence assays confirmed that Sun5 and Nesprin3 were indeed bona fide interaction partners that formed the linker of the nucleoskeleton and cytoskeleton (LINC) complex participating in the connection of the head and tail of spermatozoa.

evidence.reference_title: SUN5 Interacting With Nesprin3 Plays an Essential Role in Sperm Head-to-Tail Linkage: Research on Sun5 Gene Knockout Mice.
evidence.snippet: Nesprin3 was located posterior and anterior to the nucleus during spermiogenesis in wild-type mice, whereas it lost its localization at the implantation fossa of the posterior region in Sun5-/- mice.

evidence.reference_title: SUN5 interacts with nuclear membrane LaminB1 and cytoskeletal GTPase Septin12 mediating the sperm head-and-tail junction.
evidence.snippet: Further studies demonstrated that SUN5 connected the nucleus by interacting with LaminB1 and connected the proximal centriole by interacting with Septin12.

evidence.reference_title: The missing linker between SUN5 and PMFBP1 in sperm head-tail coupling apparatus.
evidence.snippet: We demonstrate that CENTLEIN directly interacts with both SUN5 and PMFBP1, two proteins localized in the HTCA and related with acephalic spermatozoa syndrome.

evidence.reference_title: Mechanistic insights into acephalic spermatozoa syndrome-associated mutations in the human SUN5 gene.
evidence.snippet: We also found that SUN5 interacts with the coupling apparatus protein DnaJ heat shock protein family (Hsp40) member B13 (DNAJB13) during spermatogenesis, and the substitutions in the SUN5 SUN domain impair its interaction with DNAJB13.

evidence.reference_title: SUN5 forms a regular protein lattice reinforcing the sperm head-tail junction.
evidence.snippet: By applying in situ cryoelectron tomography, we find an extensive hexagonal lattice in the nuclear envelope in this region.

nodes.description: In Sun5 knockout mice SUN5 also interacts with the mRNA export factor NXF1 and the nucleoporin NUP93, and germ cells retain poly(A) RNA in the nucleus. The authors link this to lower sperm counts and motility in the mice. Whether it contributes to the human phenotype has not been studied, and reported patients are not described as oligozoospermic, so this node has no phenotype edge.

evidence.reference_title: SUN5, a testis-specific nuclear membrane protein, participates in recruitment and export of nuclear mRNA in spermatogenesis.
evidence.snippet: In Sun5 -/- mice, the binding of Nxf1 and Nup93 decreases due to loss of Sun5 function, and the process of submitting Nxf1-binding mRNPs to Nup93 is inhibited, resulting in abnormal spermatogenesis.

nodes.description: ICSI with the detached heads or the rare intact sperm is the only route to biological paternity. A retrospective cohort reported high fertilization, good embryo quality and pregnancy in all five treated SUN5 patients, and healthy children have been born; one later family had two failed cycles.

evidence.reference_title: Patients with acephalic spermatozoa syndrome linked to SUN5 mutations have a favorable pregnancy outcome from ICSI.
evidence.snippet: The rates of fertilization, good-quality embryos and pregnancy for five patients with SUN5 mutations following ICSI were 81.5%, 81.8% and 100%, respectively.

evidence.snippet: FISH did not highlight a higher rate of chromosome aneuploidy in spermatozoa from SUN5 patients compared to controls, indicating that intra-cytoplasmic sperm injection (ICSI) can be proposed for patients carrying the c.211+1_211+2dup variant.

evidence.reference_title: Whole-exome sequencing reveals a novel mutation in the SUN5 gene causing acephalic spermatozoa syndrome.
evidence.snippet: We conducted two intracytoplasmic sperm injections (ICSI) cycles for the proband, however, the treatment did not result in his partner achieving pregnancy.

nodes.description: Nonsense, frameshift and splice-site alleles truncate SUN5 or remove its transcript, a 5-kb deletion-insertion removes exon 8, and a large deletion removes the whole gene. Several missense variants in the SUN domain alter folding and localization, and patient sperm carrying them also lack the protein. SUN5 is a testis-specific inner nuclear membrane protein that, in mature sperm, sits at the implantation fossa where the tail attaches to the head.

evidence.reference_title: Biallelic SUN5 Mutations Cause Autosomal-Recessive Acephalic Spermatozoa Syndrome.
evidence.snippet: SUN5 variants lead to absent, significantly reduced, or truncated SUN5, and certain variants altered SUN5 distribution in the head-tail junction of the sperm.

evidence.reference_title: Homozygous deletion of SUN5 in three men with decapitated spermatozoa.
evidence.snippet: We found all three men to be homozygous for a deletion-insertion variant (GRCh38 - chr20:32995761_32990672delinsTGGT) that removes 5090 base pairs including exon 8 of SUN5, predicting the frameshift, p.(Leu143Serfs*30), and the inactivation of SUN5.

evidence.reference_title: Homozygous deletion of SUN5 in three men with decapitated spermatozoa.
evidence.snippet: We also show that the p.Gly114Arg variant has a strong inhibitory effect on splicing in HeLa cells, evidence that homozygozity for p.Gly114Arg causes acephalic spermatozoa syndrome through loss of SUN5 function.

evidence.reference_title: Mechanistic insights into acephalic spermatozoa syndrome-associated mutations in the human SUN5 gene.
evidence.snippet: Furthermore, we observed that many SUN5 mutations affect the secondary structure of the protein and influence its folding and cellular localization.

evidence.reference_title: Identification and Characterization of the Most Common Genetic Variant Responsible for Acephalic Spermatozoa Syndrome in Men Originating from North Africa.
evidence.snippet: Immunofluorescence assays performed on sperm cells from three mutated subjects revealed a total absence of SUN5, thus demonstrating the deleterious impact of the identified variant on protein expression.

Healthy offspring were obtained by injecting the tail-less heads into oocytes. Independent knockout lines reproduce the phenotype.
